messages:
gabi: heads-up: a new reproducible that breaks TS inference only when bundling for edge runtimes. Node consumers fine, but Vercel/Cloudflare builds show `any` leaking from our `sdk.infer` call when a `transform` callback is passed.

len: ugh. is this the overload-vs-generic ordering problem?

gabi: looks similar but a little different. our current d.ts has three overloads for `infer` (no transform -> string, transform -> T, options-only). when bundlers resolve the ESM entry we emit re-exports that reorder things and TS picks the non-generic overload. callers end up with `Promise<any>` or `string` and lose the inferred parse type.

kevin: can you paste the simplified signatures?

gabi:```ts
export function infer(opts: { model: string }): Promise<string>;
export function infer<T>(opts: { model: string; transform: (s:string)=>T }): Promise<T>;
export function infer(opts: any): Promise<any>;
```

gabi: the local repro: set tsconfig: `module: ES2022`, `moduleResolution: "bundler"`, `target: ES2022`, and `type: module` in package.json. `tsc --noEmit` in the sample-quickstart fails to infer T.

maya: two levers: 1) collapse to a single-generic public signature `infer<T=string>(opts:{model:string; transform?: (s:string)=>T}):Promise<T>` 2) ensure package.json `exports` provides `types` subkey for the import entry so ESM consumers read the right .d.ts.

len: also consider defaulting to `unknown` instead of `any` so callers are forced to handle. we've had complaints about `any` silently propagating.

kevin: agree on `unknown`. ergonomics wise maybe `T = string` is common, but `unknown` is safer. docs can show a `parseJson<T = unknown>` helper for convenience.

gabi: short-term patch idea: 1) emit a single-generic facade d.ts that avoids overloads, 2) add `types` on the import export path, 3) add CI matrix job that runs tsc with `moduleResolution: bundler` + `module: ES2022` using both `type: module` and `type: commonjs` to catch resolver flips.

maya: +1 and include a tiny repro repo in the PR. also test with both esbuild and rollup outputs since re-export ordering differs by bundler.

len: one subtle option is `typesVersions` to force the right types for modern consumers, but I'd rather fix the emitted .d.ts shape. conditional types are another trick but can be unreadable for users.

kevin: also check our declarationMap flow. if declarationMap is missing from ESM build, TS can resolve to ambiently re-exported types in a different order. emitting consistent d.ts + map should reduce resolver nondeterminism.

ci-bot: sample-quickstart / typecheck failed on branch fix/edge-infer (see https://ci.redwood/edge/2345).

gabi: i'll open a small PR that: 1) replaces overloads with single-generic facade 2) updates package.json exports with `types` for import entry 3) adds tsc CI job 4) updates quickstart docs about `type: module` caveats.

maya: i'll review the d.ts changes. prefer `unknown` default and a clear doc comment on the signature so users understand default behavior.

len: i'll run the repro locally across ts versions (5.1/5.2/next) and with `moduleResolution: node16` vs `bundler` to ensure no regressions.

gabi: thanks all. saving this thread as the tracker. i'll attach the repro in the PR and ping when published so we can beta the fix and update quickstart to point to the patched version. :rocket:
